Hi Anna — great to hear the team liked the demo. Short answers up front, then I've attached a short worksheet with two clean scenarios.

- Proration: We prorate the incremental cost for a tier upgrade. You only pay the delta for the remainder of the billing period; the platform will show the estimated prorated charge at the time of the change.
- Feature holdback: You can opt out of the Embeddings Add-on while upgrading tiers. Embeddings is an optional add-on that can be toggled per-account; it will not block a tier upgrade. However, some Throughput-only discounts assume full-stack usage — see the workbook for the discount rows.
- Burst vs. Upgrade: If you need predictable sustained throughput (steady QPS), upgrade to Throughput. Burst credits are cheaper for short spikes but can be more expensive if used continuously. The attached workbook models both using your usage snapshot.

Attached: Carelytics_Package_Options_v1.pdf (summary + recommended path) and pricing-workbook-carelytics.xlsx (line-item math). Can you confirm the billing cadence (monthly vs annual) you prefer so I can show committed pricing?

Next step: 30-min call to walk finance through the numbers — I can do Tue/Wed afternoon PT.

Thanks for the context — read the workbook. Notes below we can reuse in our reply to procurement: 

- Feature gating: Confirmed — add-ons are togglable post-upgrade. We should call out that enabling later may require a brief provisioning step (few minutes) and could change their unit economics but won't lock them into additional seats.
- Discounting: For a first-year committed Throughput purchase we can offer up to a 12% list discount (higher only with >12 month ARR commitments or larger usage floors). If they want Embeddings excluded from the discount calc, we can structure it so the Throughput discount applies to base tokens + API calls, and Embeddings billed at list if disabled, but that reduces our ability to offer the 12% cap.
- Bursting: Recommend we show two lines in procurement email: (A) Upgrade to Throughput w/ 6-month commitment at 10% (with optional annual conversion clause), (B) Keep Compact + 10k burst credits/month (no commitment). Include estimated monthly $ for both rows.

Laura — can you draft the procurement email with those two options and the proration language? I'll add the pricing rows to the workbook.
